:::{#exr-deriv-llik-iid}
#### Derivative of the log-likelihood for $\iid$ data

For $\iid$ data,
use @thm-loglik-iid
to write the derivative $\score(\param)$ of the log-likelihood
as a sum over the observations.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#sol-deriv-llik-iid}

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lik'(\param)
&= \deriv{\param} \lik(\param)
&& \text{(notation for the derivative)}\\
&= \deriv{\param} \sumin \log{\p(X = x_i \mid \param)}
&& \text{(log-likelihood of an $\iid$ sample)}\\
&= \sumin \deriv{\param} \log{\p(X = x_i \mid \param)}
&& \text{(derivative of a sum is the sum of derivatives)}
\end{aligned}
$$

Unlike @eq-deriv-Lik, each term involves only one observation,
so no product rule is needed.

:::
